title: Cycling of Matter and Energy Flow
seo_title: Grade 7 Energy Flow Worksheets: Food Webs, Energy Pyramids and Matter Cycles
standard_text: Develop a model to describe the cycling of matter and flow of energy among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on cycling of matter and energy flow (NGSS MS-LS2-3): producers, consumers and decomposers, food webs, the 10% rule and energy pyramids, and the carbon cycle. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_sub: Energy enters from the sun and about 10% passes up each level. Decomposers return matter to the soil and air.
body_html:
How to think about it

In an ecosystem, energy flows and matter cycles.

  • Producers (plants, algae) capture energy from sunlight and make food.
  • Consumers eat producers or other consumers. Decomposers (fungi, bacteria) break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil.
  • Only about 10% of the energy at one level passes to the next; the rest is used for life processes and lost as heat. That is why an energy pyramid narrows at the top.
  • Matter (carbon, nitrogen, water) is recycled among the air, soil, water and living things.

In a food web, arrows point from the food to the eater, showing the direction energy and matter move.

Example

Producers have 5,000 units. About how much reaches the primary consumers?

10% of 5,000

Answer: 500 units

Example

Does energy get recycled?

Energy is lost as heat.

Answer: No; matter is recycled, energy flows.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy is recycled like matter.
  • Drawing arrows from predator to prey. Arrows go from food to eater.
  • Thinking top predators have the most energy.

faq.q: What is the difference between energy flow and matter cycling?
faq.a: Energy enters from the sun, flows through food chains and is lost as heat. Matter is reused again and again.
About 10% of the energy at one level of a food chain is passed to the next level. The rest is used for life processes or lost as heat.
They break down dead organisms and wastes and return nutrients to the soil and air so producers can use them again.

items.q: Luis observes: “A leaf falls and decomposers break it down.” What does this show about matter in the ecosystem?
c: Matter and energy in the grass move into the rabbit.
Nutrients return to the soil for plants to use again.
Carbon from the air becomes part of the plant.
Decomposers return carbon and nutrients to the air and soil.
items.e: Matter cycles among living and nonliving parts of the ecosystem.

items.q: What do decomposers do?
